key_insight: A stabilized Morley finite element method on polyhedral surfaces achieves optimal convergence for surface Stokes stream-function problems by exploiting a new geometric cancellation that upgrades key consistency errors from first to second order.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical, intrinsic surface PDE solver with provable accuracy for tangential flow simulation on curved geometries, which is useful in computational mechanics and multiphysics on manifolds.
method: Use an intrinsic Morley FEM directly on a piecewise linear closed-surface approximation.
Add a parameter-free jump stabilization to recover coercivity.
Prove a discrete Korn inequality and a new normal-separated geometric estimate to control surface consistency errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical optimal-order convergence under natural H3 regularity, with first order in broken H2, second order in broken H1, and second-order L2 error for recovered tangential velocity, supported by numerical experiments.
watch_item: The method relies on a polyhedral surface approximation and a delicate geometric cancellation result, so implementation and mesh geometry quality may strongly affect robustness.
paper_title: Stabilized Morley FEM for surface Stokes in stream-function formulation: Optimal convergence via a new geometric estimate
